Contributing to joinpoint

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution to joinpoint. The package implements statistical methods for trend analysis, so changes need both software-quality and statistical-methodology review.

Before You Start

  • Use GitHub issues for bug reports, feature requests, documentation gaps, and methodological questions.
  • For larger changes, open an issue first so the design can be discussed before implementation.
  • Keep pull requests focused. A statistical-method change, a documentation update, and a refactor should usually be separate pull requests.

Development Setup

Install the package dependencies from the repository root:

install.packages(c("remotes", "testthat", "devtools", "roxygen2"))
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)

The grid search is compiled C++ (through Rcpp), so you need a working C++ toolchain:

  • macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install).
  • Windows: Rtools.
  • Linux: g++ and make.

Branches and Pull Requests

  • One branch per logical change, with a name that describes it (aapc-ratio-comparison, continuous-interval-limits).
  • Write commit subjects in the imperative (“Add the jump model”). Conventional Commit prefixes are not used here.
  • Never rewrite main. git commit --amend and git push --force-with-lease are acceptable only on an unmerged branch that nobody else has pulled.
  • Keep the implementation, its tests, the roxygen source, the regenerated documentation, and the NEWS.md entry together in the same pull request.

Code Style

  • Follow the style of the surrounding R files.
  • Prefer clear validation and explicit errors over silent coercion.
  • Do not add package dependencies unless they are necessary and justified.
  • Every function and line should have a reason to exist; prefer a small, correct implementation over a general one.
  • Write documentation in American English, and cite academic papers for methods.
  • Update roxygen comments and regenerate the .Rd files together.

Testing

Run the tests while developing:

devtools::test()

Before opening a pull request, run the full check:

R CMD build .
R CMD check --as-cran joinpoint_*.tar.gz

A change to an estimator, a test, or an interval needs a test that checks the statistical output against an independent computation (brute force, lm(), glm(), or a published analysis), not only that the code runs.

Documentation

Update user-facing documentation when behavior changes:

  • roxygen examples and parameter descriptions,
  • README examples,
  • vignettes, and their rendered HTML in vignettes/ (see below),
  • NEWS.md.

Every number quoted in a vignette must match the output it accompanies; prefer inline R code for numbers in prose. To refresh the rendered vignettes:

for (f in list.files("vignettes", "\\.Rmd$", full.names = TRUE)) {
  rmarkdown::render(f, quiet = TRUE)
}

Pull Request Checklist

Before opening a pull request, confirm:

  • Tests relevant to the change pass, and R CMD check is clean.
  • Documentation is updated.
  • NEWS.md has an entry for user-facing changes.
  • No build artifacts, .Rcheck directories, compiled objects, or tarballs are committed.
  • The description explains both the software change and, when relevant, its statistical impact.

Code of Conduct

All contributors are expected to follow the project Code of Conduct.
